owner_posts.post_text:
Staying hydrated is just as important during the monsoon as it is in summer. Although the weather feels cooler, your body continues to lose fluids through daily activities. Proper hydration helps support normal body functions and overall well-being.

Here are a few simple tips to stay hydrated during the rainy season:

💧 Drink clean, safe drinking water regularly throughout the day.
🥥 Include fluids like coconut water, soups, or fresh fruit with high water content in your diet.
🍉 Eat seasonal fruits and vegetables after washing them thoroughly.
☕ Limit excessive caffeinated or sugary beverages, which may contribute to dehydration.
🧼 Carry a clean water bottle and maintain good hygiene to reduce the risk of waterborne illnesses.

Pay attention to signs such as excessive thirst, dark-colored urine, dizziness, or unusual fatigue, as these may indicate dehydration.

Maintaining healthy hydration habits, eating a balanced diet, and following good hygiene practices can help support your health during the monsoon season.

Monsoon season often brings an increase in fever-related illnesses, including dengue and viral fever. While both conditions may begin with a high temperature and body aches, they can have different causes and may require different medical evaluation.

Common signs of dengue may include:
• High fever
• Severe headache
• Pain behind the eyes
• Muscle and joint pain
• Skin rash

Common signs of viral fever may include:
• Fever with cough or sore throat
• Runny or blocked nose
• General body aches
• Fatigue

If your fever lasts more than two days, becomes very high, or is accompanied by persistent vomiting, unusual bleeding, severe weakness, or difficulty breathing, it is important to seek prompt medical attention.

Early assessment and appropriate care can help identify the underlying cause and guide suitable treatment. Staying hydrated, preventing mosquito bites, and maintaining good hygiene are important preventive measures during the monsoon season.

featured_reviews.name: ashok mukherjee
featured_reviews.review_text:
Happy experience...
Thanks doctors....

Yes my friends,
People write many nasty experience they face in hospital or with doctors. Very few write their sweet experiences in hospital or with doctors.

So I thought to share my excellent sweet experience with a small, faraway hospital but with exceptional expertise in the field of knee replacement and other orthopedic and neurological complication.

My wife Operated for knee replacement on 15th...At 11 in the morning (to 2.30 pm) including recovery time inside operation theatre...

Then shifted to ICU.
Operation was good, my wife was in jolly mood and smiling while coming out from OT after the replacement ... But after 2 hrs of shifting to ICU, the real pain started... Wife was crying like mad for pain... But through medication by 8 pm it has started reducing... and she slept.
Nxt day, 16th, morning no pain...and shifted to pvt room cabin. I also staying in the same room with her. Excellent clean cosy room with all necessary requirements like AC, TV, eye catching view from 4th floor Window, attached very clean bath (no balcony), clean and daily fresh linen.

17th.. Sr Doctors and physiotherapist started her to walk and bent the new knee to 90°...

This was regular exercise, bending knee to 90° and walking in the corridor with the help of walker and physiotherapist till 19th...

And on 19th all bandage and all drain-pipes ( 3 in total... For Blood to drain our excess blood at operated knee, one for urine, one at spinal joint to push different medicine ) removed and....
discharged in the afternoon by doctor...
Same day, 19th, came to home by evening.

She is recovering nicely.... Walking inside the flat with the help of walker... pain she feel very very rarely.

After 9th day from operation, today (24th March) was the first check up...and it is absolutely OK.
Infact, my wife walk through out the day in hospital alone with the help of walker.
Today, she has been allowed by doctor to move and do morning/evening walk with walker and asked for further check up after 15 days.
No medicine given except multivitamin for further recovery as she has no pain.

We are very very happy for the excellent smooth operation, expertise of doctors, quick recovery process with effective treatment, support of Jr. Doctors, Physiotherapist, Metron, Sisters, Brothers, room boy and aayas for 24×7 and overall management of the hospital.

Well behaved people....
No extra billing...

We, and no one, before surgery, expected that after operation on 2nd day pain would vanish... she would walk and bend knee to 90°and get discharge on 4th day...!!!

All credit goes to Dr. Rahul Bade and his team including Anesthesists Dr. Ganesh Kolhe at Sparsh Multi-Speciality Hospital.

Thank you...well done, doctor !!!
🙏🙏🙏

Thanks to Lt. Col Dr Amogh Yadav from Mumbai and Dr. Rahul Mane for strongly recomanding us the hospital.

(Note : Treatment was going on at Sanchiti Hospital. But operated at Sparsh Multi Speciality Hospital)

featured_reviews.name: Nidhi Patel
featured_reviews.review_text:
We had an extremely distressing experience at Siddhachal Hospital, Prabhadevi, after our elderly family member was admitted there in an emergency with a fracture on her left hip. I would strongly advise against choosing this hospital, especially for elderly patients or anyone needing urgent, attentive care.

From the moment we arrived, the facility was poorly equipped, lacking even a decent waiting area. The treatment was abysmal — staff showed no understanding of pain management, administering painkillers randomly without clear guidance or monitoring. The response time was shockingly slow, and even basic infrastructure like Wi-Fi was dysfunctional, with internet speeds so slow that documentation took ages, directly delaying care.

Throughout our time there, staff were often seen gossiping instead of attending to patients, adding to the frustration and anxiety of an already difficult situation. When we decided to shift our grandmother to another hospital due to their incompetence, staff delayed the transfer unnecessarily, questioning our decision rather than focusing on a safe and swift discharge.

The ambulance service was unprofessional and unsafe:

We had requested to go to their Lower Parel branch, but were wrongly brought to Prabhadevi.

The ambulance staff had no clue how to properly lift a patient with a hip fracture, lacked the strength needed, and mishandled her during transfers.

The ambulance light kept flickering uncontrollably while going over speed bumps, creating an alarming and chaotic environment.

There was nothing positive about this experience. From slow internet hampering documentation to staff gossiping instead of caring for patients, every aspect of the stay was marked by carelessness, inefficiency, and a lack of empathy.

I strongly recommend avoiding Siddhachal Hospital, Prabhadevi. The hospital’s systems, infrastructure, staff training, and attitude are completely inadequate for providing safe and dignified care.

featured_reviews.review_text: I had a great experience at this hospital. The service provided was excellent, and the staff were very polite, supportive, and always ready to help. featured_reviews.review_text:

To the team at Fortis Hospital led by Dr Boman your support and professionalism was amazing and top notch..Thanks to Drs Boman, Subhaprakah, Kirti, Priyinka, Sanyal, Burmarji, Kothari, Rupal, Meena, Aisha, Tejas, Vijay, Sindhuja, Siska, Uma,Brushali, Bebykumari, Aarthi and Trisha the Nutrition Therapist and the nurses, you were a blessing and being there to support, review and advise in a very timely manner and professionally.

featured_reviews.name: Augustine Wassago
featured_reviews.review_text: My wife and I accompanied our son Daudi for medical attention to India early January 2020. The team at Magnus Medi supported us with visa info, arranged airport pickup and drop off, provided sim-cards to ease our communication, made appointments for us and visited us regularly at the hospital to ensure we felt home. Indeed, we felt at home indeed. You are an excellent team and permit my wife and I to very deeply thank Sanket, Madga and Judith who made our entire journey and stay in Mumbai as comfortable as possible. God bless you beyond measure.

featured_reviews.name: Farhat Rajput
featured_reviews.review_text:
I Farhat Begum from Kenya visited Nanavati Max hospital in Mumbai in October 2022 for a medical check up. With assistance from Mr Tarandeep and the international team at Nanavati Max welcomed us well, understood our needs and took us through the entire process smoothly. Upon medical findings, I was diagnosed with PCOS and a polyp growth in my uterus.
We decided to travel back in Jan 2023 for the surgical procedure. During that time the international team assisted us with all requirements, answered our endless queries that built our confidence to trust them with our health matters.
Dr. Chaitali Trivedi and her team were very reassuring that all will be well. They were very kind and courteous during the whole process that made me feel safe and thank God all went well with minimal post operation pains. I am greatful for the entire team for coming togather and making this medical journey easier for me.

Once again Thank you Mr. Tarandeep, Dr. Chaitali Trivedi and Nanavati Max team.

You are doing a wonderful job and please keep it up and God will reward you.
I wish you all the best.
